meta.description: Sends a personalised email to the applicants that have new results. The email always goes to an address of the allow list, never to the address of the applicant file. The request is answered at once, so the mail server never holds the matching back.

nodes.name: Acknowledge Request
nodes.notes: The request is answered at once. The mails are sent in the background, so a slow mail server never holds the matching back.

parameters.query:
WITH recipients AS (
  SELECT coalesce(array_agg(address ORDER BY address), ARRAY[]::text[]) AS addresses
  FROM notification_recipients
  WHERE active
),
decisions AS (
  SELECT
    d.user_id,
    d.product_id,
    d.lane,
    d.status,
    d.reasons,
    m.decided_by,
    m.score,
    m.llm_assessment,
    u.name,
    u.email,
    u.age,
    u.monthly_income,
    u.credit_score,
    u.employment_status,
    u.batch_id,
    p.product_name,
    p.provider,
    p.interest_rate_min,
    p.interest_rate_max,
    p.min_loan_amount,
    p.max_loan_amount,
    p.min_tenure_months,
    p.max_tenure_months
  FROM ui_decisions d
  JOIN users u ON u.user_id = d.user_id
  JOIN loan_products p ON p.product_id = d.product_id
  LEFT JOIN matches m ON m.batch_id = d.batch_id AND m.user_id = d.user_id AND m.product_id = d.product_id
  WHERE d.batch_id = '{{ $('Validate Request').first().json.batch_id }}'::uuid
    AND p.active
    AND d.status IN ('eligible', 'review', 'pending')
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM notifications n
      WHERE n.user_id = d.user_id AND n.batch_id = d.batch_id AND n.status <> 'failed'
    )
)
SELECT
  decisions.*,
  (SELECT addresses FROM recipients) AS allowed_recipients
FROM (SELECT 1 AS one) AS anchor
LEFT JOIN decisions ON TRUE
ORDER BY decisions.user_id NULLS FIRST, decisions.interest_rate_min NULLS LAST, decisions.product_name

nodes.name: Fetch Matched Applicants
nodes.notes: The decisions of the batch: the confirmed eligibility and the requests for missing information, plus the addresses that are allowed to receive a notification.  An applicant that was already notified about this batch is skipped, so a repeated dispatch never sends the same mail twice.

nodes.name: Build Notification Emails
nodes.notes: One personalised email per applicant, addressed to the allow list.

nodes.name: Send Notification
nodes.notes: Local run goes to Mailpit, in production the same credential points at the SMTP endpoint of Amazon SES.

parameters.query:
WITH written AS (
  INSERT INTO notifications (
    user_id, batch_id, match_count, review_count, recipient, provider, status,
    provider_message_id, error, sent_at
  )
  SELECT
    t.user_id,
    t.batch_id,
    t.match_count,
    t.review_count,
    t.recipient,
    t.provider,
    t.status,
    t.provider_message_id,
    t.error,
    CASE WHEN t.status = 'sent' THEN NOW() ELSE NULL END
  FROM jsonb_to_recordset({{ $json.notifications_sql }}::jsonb) AS t(
    user_id text, batch_id uuid, match_count int, review_count int, recipient text,
    provider text, status text, provider_message_id text, error text
  )
  ON CONFLICT (user_id, batch_id) WHERE batch_id IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET
    match_count = EXCLUDED.match_count,
    review_count = EXCLUDED.review_count,
    recipient = EXCLUDED.recipient,
    status = EXCLUDED.status,
    provider_message_id = EXCLUDED.provider_message_id,
    error = EXCLUDED.error,
    sent_at = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.status = 'sent' THEN NOW() ELSE NULL END
  RETURNING notification_id, status
),
finished AS (
  UPDATE ingestion_batches SET notifications_completed_at = NOW()
  WHERE batch_id = '{{ $('Validate Request').first().json.batch_id }}'::uuid
  RETURNING batch_id
),
duration AS (
  UPDATE matching_runs r
  SET notifications_ms = (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (clock_timestamp() -
        '{{ $('Validate Request').first().json.requested_at }}'::timestamptz)) * 1000)::bigint
  WHERE r.run_id = (
    SELECT run_id FROM matching_runs
    WHERE batch_id = '{{ $('Validate Request').first().json.batch_id }}'::uuid
    ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1)
  RETURNING run_id
)
SELECT
  count(*)::int AS notifications_written,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'sent')::int AS notifications_sent,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed')::int AS notifications_failed,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM finished)::int AS batches_finished,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM duration)::int AS durations_written
FROM written

nodes.name: Record Notifications
nodes.notes: One row per applicant and batch, so a repeated dispatch never sends or records the same mail twice.
